report.reference: McShane LM et al. J Natl Cancer Inst 2005;97:1180-4; Altman DG et al. PLoS Med 2012;9:e1001216
report.methods: Candidate markers (n = 30) were screened for association with time / event in 260 patients (151 events) with SurvStudio 0.4.0.dev0. Each marker was tested for added value over the clinical covariates (z, grade, binary) with a Cox score test against the model with the clinical covariates alone, using the Efron method for tied event times. Multiplicity was assessed with Westfall-Young step-down max-T p-values from 99 permutations; for added value, the residuals of each marker after regression on the clinical covariates were permuted (Smith method; Winkler et al. 2014), approximating a conditional null under exchangeable residuals after linear adjustment, and the false discovery rate was estimated from the same permutations. Permutation inference requires exchangeability under the chosen null; strong family-wise error control also requires subset pivotality. Nonlinear marker-covariate relations can invalidate the residual-permutation calibration. Added-value testing also requires a suitable clinical Cox baseline: its functional form and proportional-hazards assumptions need checking. Multiplicity adjustment does not establish model adequacy. The whole screening procedure was repeated on 4 event-stratified subsamples of 63.2% of the patients; in each, a marker counted as selected when its Benjamini-Hochberg q-value was at most 0.05, and its rank and direction were recorded. A marker was robust when its family-wise p-value was at most 0.05, it was selected in at least 50% of the subsamples and its direction held in at least 90% of them; markers with a family-wise p-value at most 0.05 or a permutation q-value at most 0.1 that did not meet the stability rule were called suggestive, and markers without sufficient evidence of added value but with a marginal family-wise p-value at most 0.05 were called marginal only. Markers with more than 20% missing values, a constant value or more than 90% of patients at one value were excluded before testing (a filter blind to the outcome); other missing marker values were replaced by the marker's median among the patients in each fit, and patients with a missing or invalid outcome or stratum were excluded; missing clinical values used training-only imputation. Markers were analysed as continuous variables without cut-points. Patients with identical values on every marker were flagged as possible repeated samples; near-identical profiles are checked only on panels of at least 200 markers. A Cox model with the clinical covariates and the selected markers (at most the 10 strongest) was fitted, and its apparent C-index was adjusted for the subsampling gap by subtracting the mean difference between the C-index of the whole procedure in each subsample and in the patients left out of it; this heuristic includes training-size effects. In the patients left out of each subsample, the C-index of the model fitted in that subsample was compared with that of a Cox model of the clinical covariates alone fitted in the same subsample; the 95% confidence interval of the mean difference used the approximate corrected resampled t statistic (Nadeau and Bengio 2003), which accounts for overlap between subsamples under its covariance assumptions. Coverage for this survival selection procedure has not been established. Clinical basis: linear; training-only imputation, encoding and fixed knots were refitted in each training subset. Clinical PH/functional-form diagnostics and all-marker residual HC3 mean/variance diagnostics formed separate Holm families, with withholding at 1%. Method version marker-inference/2; inference status assumption_dependent. Inference depends on model and permutation assumptions; diagnostics do not certify them.
report.results: Of 30 markers, 1 was robust, 0 suggestive and 0 marginal only. The selected-marker model (m0) had an apparent C-index of 0.777 and a subsample gap-adjusted C-index of 0.769. In the patients left out of each of 4 subsamples, the whole selection procedure reached a mean C-index of 0.767 against 0.620 for the clinical covariates alone (mean difference +0.148, 95% CI 0.080 to 0.215). Markers were selected and models refitted in each subsample; validate the locked final model independently. Finite main-study engineering gates in prespecified supported conditions; not universal 5% error control or certification of an individual dataset. The 500-subject, 300-marker and 3000-marker extensions do not establish broader qualification. In particular, large independent and linear marker families substantially reduce availability; power retention and conditional error bounds also remain limiting. The screen for repeated samples flagged no patients.

items.text: No marker was marginal only (associated with survival on its own but adding nothing beyond the clinical covariates). Show how the reported markers relate to the standard prognostic variables.

The marker table gives every marker's unadjusted score-test p-value (Unadjusted P) and, for all 30 markers, the hazard ratio from an unadjusted Cox model as a point estimate (Unadjusted HR); the table's confidence intervals belong to the adjusted hazard ratios. Kaplan-Meier curves by marker level can be drawn in the Survival curves tab with a cut-point fixed in advance.

The marker table gives, for all 30 markers, hazard ratios with 95% Wald confidence intervals from Cox models with the clinical covariates. Report the final model with all its variables from the Cox model tab.

items.topic: Further investigations: assumptions, sensitivity, internal validation
items.text: Internal validation: the whole procedure was repeated on 4 subsamples; the selected-marker model's apparent C-index was 0.777 and its heuristic subsample gap-adjusted C-index was 0.769; in the patients left out, the log hazard ratio of each subsample's strongest marker (the one with the largest score statistic, whether or not it was selected) was on average 122.1% of its value in the subsample. In the patients left out of each of 4 subsamples, the whole selection procedure reached a mean C-index of 0.767 against 0.620 for the clinical covariates alone (mean difference +0.148, 95% CI 0.080 to 0.215). Markers were selected and models refitted in each subsample; validate the locked final model independently. Check proportional hazards for the reported markers in the Cox model tab.
